vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: douyin-transcribe
Version: 1.0.0

The skill is designed to transcribe Douyin videos using Groq's Whisper API, but it contains significant shell injection vulnerabilities. In `scripts/transcribe.js`, the `runCommand` function uses `execSync` with unsanitized string interpolation for URLs and file paths, which could allow arbitrary command execution if the AI agent is manipulated into passing malicious input. While the behavior aligns with the stated purpose and no evidence of intentional data exfiltration or backdoors was found, the high-risk implementation of shell commands warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's stated registry metadata omits several real requirements (GROQ API key, ffmpeg, browser tool) and asks the user to paste their Groq API key into chat and to let the agent modify a local .env file — these mismatches and secret-handling instructions are inconsistent and warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims no required env vars or binaries in the top-level registry metadata, but both SKILL.md and _meta.json clearly require ffmpeg, a Groq API key, and agent browser/exec/read tools. The code (scripts/transcribe.js) also depends on these. The mismatch between declared requirements and actual runtime needs is incoherent — a user installing based on registry info would be surprised to need a Groq key and ffmpeg.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read the skill .env, copy .env.example to .env if missing, run shell commands (ffmpeg -version), start/navigate a browser and evaluate page JS to extract an audio URL, then set environment variables and invoke node scripts. Those actions are consistent with the stated purpose (extract audio and transcribe), but asking the user to paste their Groq API key into chat and to let the agent write it into .env exposes secrets via chat and gives the agent the ability to modify files in the skill directory. Reading/modifying only the skill's own .env is expected, but the instruction to have users send an API key in-chat is risky and should be called out.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote install spec is present and the skill includes a local script file. There are no downloads from arbitrary URLs during install. The execution model is instruction-driven and runs local Node.js code; this is proportionate to the feature and is lower risk than a skill that fetches and executes code at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Although the registry metadata lists no required env vars, the skill requires GROQ_API_KEY (and optionally OPENAI_API_KEY) according to SKILL.md and the script. Requesting a free Groq API key is plausible for transcription, but the skill's instructions ask the user to paste the key into chat so the agent can 'help set it up' — this exposes a secret via conversation and gives the agent write-access to a local .env. That level of secret handling should have been declared upfront. The skill also reads optional cookies and may use yt-dlp if browser extraction fails; that may touch cookies files if present.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true and is user-invocable. It asks to write/update its own .env and create output/temp directories (normal for this functionality). It does not request elevated or system-wide configuration changes. No other skills' configs are modified in the instructions or code.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says (open Douyin, extract audio, run ffmpeg, call Groq for STT and post-processing), but there are important inconsistencies and privacy risks to consider:

- The registry metadata did not declare required items, but the skill actually needs ffmpeg and a GROQ_API_KEY. Expect to install ffmpeg and supply a Groq key in a local .env.
- The SKILL.md asks you to paste your Groq API key into chat so the agent can write it into .env. Avoid pasting sensitive API keys into general chat if you don't trust the skill/agent environment — prefer manually editing the .env file yourself.
- The skill will run local commands (ffmpeg, ffprobe, optionally yt-dlp) and will create/read files under the skill directory (temp/, douyin-transcripts/, .env). Review the included scripts/transcribe.js before use to confirm behavior and endpoints it calls (it uses HTTPS to contact external APIs). If you are not comfortable, run the script manually from a terminal rather than letting the agent run it autonomously.
- If you allow the agent browser tool to open Douyin, be aware it may rely on the agent's browser session (which could contain logged-in cookies). If you have sensitive sessions, consider extracting audio locally instead of using the browser mode.

What would change this assessment: a registry update that accurately lists required env vars/tools (GROQ_API_KEY, ffmpeg, browser), and SKILL.md guidance that instructs the user to manually place the key into .env (rather than pasting it in chat). If you want to proceed, prefer manual configuration (copy .env.example and add GROQ_API_KEY locally) and run the transcribe script yourself or review the code first.
